Recurrence: with no premise and no decidability, a list holding the first l.length + 1 values of a sequence holds two equal ones, so a sequence that never revisits has no list holding it; a quantity that never falls and rises across every change stops change within finitely many configurations; under a determined law a lost possibility stays lost and merged configurations stay merged, and where a list holds every configuration, merging nothing, every configuration returning and every configuration reachable at every step are one, a rise along an orbit needs a merge and a merge loses a possibility for good, while counting on and counting down separate the three in an open world; keeping its history every law merges nothing, never returns, cannot have its beginning again and has no list holding it, and within finitely many configurations two histories share one present from every step on. Renewal: a run read through observables of conditions is one relational unfolding; an observable that never rises from some step on falls only finitely often, with depletion, recurrent renewal under a natural-number rank and unrenewed drawdown as its cases; in one process from one configuration one run renews and another consumes. Dependence: which conditions a formation depends on, at what level, and which it draws on may change from step to step; constant dependence recovers the static reading exactly; every met dependence is kept or broken across each step; consumption as inherited admits a requirement never met, which consumes its condition with no break; where activity needs current support, a formation still active after a loss without return has weakened or dissolved its dependence, and with fixed dependence it is no longer active, both contrapositives of that premise; these outcomes are neither exhaustive nor exclusive, and in one process from one configuration a break of the same dependence, read at the start of its step, is followed by an ending, a transformation and a restoration; an event is within renewal when its step keeps every dependence on the conditions it participates in, breaking when it draws on a condition at a step that breaks a dependence on it, and undermining when it draws on a condition at a step after which the condition is below both the present need of a dependence on it and a need of that dependence met at some step of its tenure, so that a level from before the dependence held and a dependence never met at its own need do not count, falling short only of a need grown beyond what was met is not undermining, a draw below a need that was met undermines after the need has grown, and a dependence that lapses for one step starts a new tenure; breaking is undermining, drawing after a loss can undermine without breaking, and drawing that changes no level can undermine; the stepwise and whole-run readings credit different events in both directions; the lemmas on natural numbers the layers share are stated here. Return: a dependence returns within p steps when it is met at one of the next p; renewal, renewal within one step, within p, return and non-consumption are ordered, and consumption is exactly a dependence that never returns; renewal within one step does not imply renewal, and cycles of length zero are degenerate; a seasonal condition is renewed within two steps and not one; a recovery can slow without bound, returning always while no cycle bounds it; over cycles of two a dip is credited, and an escalation undermines for every cycle. Horizon: for every horizon two runs of one process agree up to it, drawing beyond renewal with every event within renewal, and afterwards one renews and the other consumes; a reading decided by a finite prefix that credits every renewing run credits a consuming one; the renewing run itself draws beyond renewal before the horizon and the whole-run reading credits it; a reading of amounts per step is fixed by the history through the step and withholds every such draw; the formation-level cycle readings are not fixed by any finite prefix; and the same holds in the support-gated law, whose renewal stops below support.
